correctness.rationale: On R_n=K_n square K_n, the closed-neighborhood sum is r_i+c_j-x_ij. Weight W<2n implies some row r_i<=1 and some column c_j<=1, whose intersection has x_ij<=1 and closed sum <=2, contradiction. At W=2n a row sum 0 would force all columns >=3, while row sum 1 forces all other columns >=2 and one >=3, impossible; symmetry gives all row and column sums exactly 2. Conversely each nonnegative matrix of margins 2 has entries <=2 and valid constrained neighborhood sums 4 (zeros), 3 (ones). Every matrix decomposes into two permutation matrices; cycles of P^{-1}Q of length>=2 contribute two alternating decompositions, giving M_n=n! sum_pi 2^{-c_>=2(pi)}=(n!)^2[z^n] e^{z/2}/sqrt(1-z). Independent bounded-weight exhaustive labels at n=2,3,4 gave 3,21,282 minimizers with correct margins; symbolic proof handles every n>=3.
